quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers and pedestrians. Sound it immediately if you think another car will hit you.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers in the intersection.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, you should:

options.text: Wait until you can clearly see all tracks before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can clearly see all tracks before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming from the other direction.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
Anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right if a car is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane. You can also pass on the right on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass.

questions.question: In ideal driving conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?

options.text: Four seconds.
500 feet.
Six seconds.
300 yards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: In ideal conditions, keep at least four seconds between your car and the car ahead. Increase this distance in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Over-the-counter allergy and cold medicine
Prescription pain medicine
Illegal drugs
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug, including over-the-counter medicine, prescription medicine, and illegal drugs. The penalties are the same as for drunk driving. Check how any new medicine affects driving before you drive.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A community group is picking up trash ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: When facing bright headlights from an oncoming car, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has high beams on, look toward the right edge of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright lights.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very rare.
Extremely dangerous.
Not a serious problem.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Stay focused on the road to prevent crashes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate the curves.

questions.question: You should slow down, yield, and be ready to stop for pedestrians:

options.text: Only when a traffic light is yellow or red.
When they are crossing or walking on the road.
Only when they are in marked crosswalks.
Only when they are crossing the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are crossing or walking on the road.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. You must yield to pedestrians, even if they are not following the rules.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that a red light is coming. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher risk of crashing when using which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you from driving and increase your crash risk.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Let other road users know what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other road users know what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by using turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when needed.

questions.question: Statistics show that alcohol is:

options.text: A factor in almost half of all fatal traffic crashes.
Rarely involved in traffic crashes.
The cause of all traffic crashes.
Involved only in crashes with no deaths.

questions.correctAnswerText: A factor in almost half of all fatal traffic crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many deaths in traffic crashes. About 45 percent of all traffic deaths involve alcohol.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them feel normal again?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol in your body.

questions.question: You are stopped at a railroad crossing where a train just passed. You should:

options.text: Look and listen for another train. Cross only when the tracks are clear.
Assume no other trains are coming.
Start crossing the tracks quickly.
Wait 20 seconds before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen for another train. Cross only when the tracks are clear.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, check for trains coming from either direction on other tracks. Only cross when you are sure the tracks are clear.

questions.question: If you refuse to take a chemical test when asked by police:

options.text: 10 points will be added to your license record.
Your license will be revoked.
You will be charged with a crime.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Refusing a chemical test results in two criminal charges: DUI and Refusal. Your license will be revoked, and 10 points will be added to your record.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right goes first.
The driver on the left goes first.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right goes first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You should yield and go when it is safe.
